title: Ticketed Launch Pocket Guide & Burn Radar
body:
Ticketed Launch Pocket Guide — Burn Radar & KPI Matrix

Purpose:
A compact operational checklist and lightweight simulator to 1) gate traffic by ticketed thresholds, 2) predict immediate capacity burn under surge scenarios, and 3) map fast mitigations for the hosted API feature 'smart routing v2' canary rollout. This is intentionally short-form for on-call and launch-day owners.

Scope:
- Applies to staged rollouts for new routing and batching policies on hosted-api and dedicated tiers.
- Primary focus: latency SLOs, token cost run-rate, and failed-request escalation thresholds during the first 72 hours after canary widening.
- Not a replacement for full launch playbooks — this is the quick-run reference for product-ops & on-call SRE.

Quick checklist (ticketed flow):
- Ticket creation: PRODOPS-734 (owner: Asha) — attach smoke test results and baseline KPIs.
- Pre-rollout (T-72 to T-1): verify canary WFM, KV cache priming, BDD + load smoke (2 x baseline).
- Canary Day (T0): open incident channel (#launch-smart-routing), standby owners: eng-oncall, infra-gpu, product-ops.
- Gate tickets at each traffic step: ticket comment must include KPIs snapshot, run-rate, and fallback decision.
- Post-rollout (T+72): run regression tests, token-cost analysis, and post-launch retro.

KPI Burn Radar (single-line table for quick scan):
KPI | Target | Green | Yellow | Red | Owner
- 99th_token_latency_ms | <= 220ms | <= 240ms | 240-320ms | >320ms | SRE
- Median_latency_ms | <= 55ms | <= 80ms | 80-140ms | >140ms | Serving-runtime
- Error_rate_pct | <0.4% | <1.0% | 1.0-3.0% | >3.0% | Infra
- Tokens_per_minute (system) | baseline | +25% | +25-200% | >200% | Product-ops
- Unit_token_cost_usd | baseline | -5% to +10% | +10-40% | >+40% | Finance/Ops

Runway Burn Simulator (assumptions + outcomes):
Assumptions: baseline traffic = 100k tokens/min, baseline GPU pool = 12 devices (A100-equivalent), avg token cost = $0.00016.
Scenarios (rounded):
- Baseline (1x): 100k tpm -> expected latency green, cost ~ $9.6/hr.
- Moderate Surge (2.5x): 250k tpm -> batching efficiency improves per-token but KV pressure increases. Estimated needed GPUs: 28; cost ~ $22.6/hr; risk: yellow (queueing 5-10ms). Action: enable burst pool +40% and tighten prefix caching TTL.
- Large Surge (5x): 500k tpm -> estimated GPUs: 52; cost ~ $42/hr; risk: red (99p >320ms, error_rate climb). Action: throttle non-critical routes, enable fallback model variant (quantized), and open inc channel.
- Flash (10x): 1,000k tpm -> estimated GPUs: 95+; cost ~ $78/hr (sustained). Action: immediate traffic hold for ticketed customers, global fallback to low-cost region, escalate to exec.

Notes on model variants & fallback economics:
- Primary (full-precision) -> fallback #1 (int8 quant) -> fallback #2 (smaller-llm). Each step reduces per-token latency/cost, but increases hallucination risk. Map fallback order into ticket comments and pre-approved rollback conditions.

Traffic Gating Rules (ticket thresholds):
- Gate 1 (canary widen 10% -> 25%): continue if 99p_latency <= 240ms AND error_rate < 1.0%.
- Gate 2 (25% -> 60%): continue if tokens_per_minute delta < +150% vs baseline and unit_cost_delta < +20%.
- Gate 3 (60% -> 100%): require SRE signoff OR automatic throttles + fallback engaged if tokens delta > +200% OR 99p_latency > 320ms for 3 consecutive samples (1 min).

Immediate mitigation steps (first 10 minutes):
1) Flip per-route fallbacks to quantized variant (pre-deployed). 2) Reduce max_tokens for non-essential API endpoints by 30%. 3) Scale burst capacity (if available) by +40% via Dedicated autoscale policy. 4) If error rate climbs >3%: execute partial rollback (traffic cut from 60% to 20%) and open postmortem ticket.

Communication playbook (who says what):
- Incident owner (SRE): real-time KPI snapshots to #launch-smart-routing every 5m; update ticket with decision.
- Product-ops (Asha): summary cadence (T+15, T+30, T+60) to stakeholders; confirm fallback steps and customer notifications.
- Support triage: prepare templated customer-facing message if degradation > yellow for >30m.

Post-launch evaluation & success markers (T+72):
- Primary success: sustained 99p_latency <= 240ms and error_rate <1% on production traffic for 72 hours.
- Cost success: unit_token_cost delta <= +10% vs baseline after batching and cache savings.
- Quality guardrail: no measurable regression on top-100 eval prompts (A/B).

Owners matrix (short):
- Launch owner: Asha Patel (product-ops).
- SRE lead: Ethan Ruiz.
- Serving runtime: Maya Chen.
- Infra/GPU ops: Liam O'Connor.

Linked tickets & quick links:
- PRODOPS-734: canary plan and smoke results.
- SERVE-1293: fallback variant pre-deploy.
- FIN-201: cost estimation spreadsheet (link in linked_artifacts).

Open questions (to capture in the ticket):
- Are regional fallbacks legally allowed for the set of enterprise customers in the canary cohort? (legal/product verification)
- Should we auto-scale burst GPUs above reserved capacity or rely on throttles first?

How to use this sheet on-call:
- Bookmark this doc and the ticket. For any Gate fail, comment on ticket with the four datapoints: 99p latency, median latency, error rate, tokens/min. If two of four are in Yellow or any in Red, execute mitigation decision tree and update ticket.

Appendix: quick templated messages
- Customer-facing: "We are observing intermittent latency and are routing your requests to a stable variant; no data loss expected. Engineering is actively investigating."
- Stakeholder update (T+30): snapshot of the four KPIs, mitigation steps executed, and next decision timestamp.

End of pocket guide. Keep this short doc attached to the launch ticket and use it as the canonical first-response checklist.
